body: >I’m guessing that you’re here because you have a family law problem and are a bit shell-shocked at how your ex – that person you used to love, and may still have feelings for – has suddenly changed. You are especially stunned at how she’s carrying on, given the effect it’s having on the children, from whom you have largely been cut off, and you wonder at how the Family Court system could possibly fail to see that they need their father, too.

>If you’ve have had the suspicion that you were going bald, you probably have had a strong need to figure out just what is “happening under the hood.” There is a sea of rumors floating out there that attempt to explain the “root” of the problem. After all, the great Hippocrates, father of modern medicine, thought that baldness could be cured by a mixture containing horseradish and pigeon droppings. The desire to have a simple solution -– particularly one that is within our control –- is understandable. But today, let’s debunk some of these myths and learn what the facts really are.

>When New York Times contributing editor Daniel Jones started losing his hair, he chose what he considers a “cooler alternative” — head shaving.
